what: Cloudflare runs a global network that sits in front of websites and applications. It blocks attacks, speeds up delivery, provides corporate network security and increasingly runs customers' code and AI workloads at the edge.
customers: Websites and apps of every size, from free users to large enterprises; corporate IT and security teams.
money: security, performance and developer platform subscriptions, mostly annual contracts
moat: A network present in hundreds of cities that would be very expensive to reproduce, plus the data advantage of seeing a large share of the world's internet traffic.
risks: It is not yet profitable on reported earnings and lost about $239 million over the last twelve months
The shares trade at a very high multiple of revenue, which leaves no room for a growth slowdown
Large cloud providers bundle competing services
Winning large enterprise contracts takes long sales cycles
opportunities: Revenue has grown about 30% a year while gross margins stay around 75%
The developer platform and AI inference at the edge open markets beyond security
Large customers spending over $100,000 a year are the fastest-growing group
watch: Dollar-based net retention and the number of large customers, which show whether existing accounts keep expanding.
